urban.population_and_unit: U.S. adults age 18 and older; percent reporting household food insecurity
urban.geography_and_period: United States; December 2025; household food insecurity in the last 12 months
urban.instrument_and_method: Urban Institute normalized figures from the December 2025 WBNS release; the 2025 sample expanded to include adults age 65 and older and the publication reports an updated estimation approach.
uncertainty_and_limits: WBNS is an annual survey of adults and is not numerically interchangeable with USDA's CPS household series.
The 2025 methodology update means estimates differ slightly from earlier Urban publications; preserve the publication's definitions and significance annotations.
The survey has a low cumulative response rate and may underrepresent people experiencing homelessness, low literacy, or limited English/Spanish proficiency.
The figures describe reported household food insecurity, not provider utilization, capacity, revenue, or company demand.

usda.population_and_unit: percent of households food insecure at some time during the year
usda.geography_and_period: U.S. Department of Agriculture Economic Research Service, Household Food Security in the United States; 2022-2023 construction and 2024 holdout
usda.instrument_and_method: Annual CPS Food Security Supplement household survey
uncertainty_and_limits: Food insecurity rose numerically from 2022 through the 2024 holdout, but USDA reports the 2024 prevalence was not statistically significantly different from 2023 or 2022.
This is a descriptive repeated-cross-section holdout from one USDA survey family. It is not a causal or independent validation result.

independence_assessment.assessment: Distinct publisher families provide a directional challenge, but different populations, denominators, uncertainty treatment, and method details prevent a common estimate or independent confirmation claim.
